description: Remove legacy crypto* compatibility layers introduced during Feature-13 after the deprecation window, making bitcoin* naming the only supported runtime, packaging, and documentation surface.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed only after deprecation window ends and no critical users depend on legacy aliases.

principles: Finalize the Canonical Surface - bitcoin* names become the only supported names
No Silent Breakage - removal must be announced clearly with migration guidance
Deterministic Cleanup - remove all shims, aliases, and fallback branches in one coordinated pass
Data Safety First - do not break existing databases or data access paths without explicit migration path
Keep Scope Tight - cleanup legacy naming only; defer unrelated refactors

userStories.title: Remove legacy module shims
acceptanceCriteria: Delete legacy shim modules: src/python/cryptoAccounts.py, src/python/cryptoAccounting.py, and top-level cryptoAccounting.py
Remove legacy alias exports tied to compatibility-only behavior where safe
Canonical modules bitcoinAccounts.py and bitcoinAccounting.py remain fully functional
Tests and imports are updated to avoid any dependency on legacy module names

userStories.title: Remove legacy console script aliases
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml keeps only canonical script target(s) for Bitcoin naming
Remove crypto-accounting and crypto-tui alias entries
README and GETTING_STARTED remove legacy command references

userStories.title: Finalize data path policy
acceptanceCriteria: Decide and document whether legacy fallback to ~/.cryptoaccounting remains or is removed
If removed: get_sqlite_path() defaults exclusively to ~/.bitcoinaccounting unless SQLITE_DB_PATH is set
If retained: docs clearly define long-term support policy for legacy path fallback
Tests reflect the final policy and pass deterministically

userStories.title: Purge legacy language from docs and scripts
acceptanceCriteria: README, GETTING_STARTED, .env.example, and script headers contain no legacy crypto* identity references
Migration section is updated from compatibility mode to historical note or removed
Deprecation timeline is reflected as completed with concrete dates

userStories.title: Cleanup tests and planning metadata
acceptanceCriteria: Update or remove compatibility tests that intentionally reference legacy modules/commands
Update planning/current-feature.json, planning/progress.txt, and AGENTS.md with cleanup learnings
userStories.testStrategy: pytest targeted suites + planning artifact validation

high: Breaking external scripts still importing cryptoAccounts after aliases are removed
Unexpected operational disruption if legacy CLI aliases are removed before users update automation
medium: Path fallback removal can confuse users who still rely on ~/.cryptoaccounting
Documentation drift during transition from compatibility mode to canonical-only mode
low: Most cleanup is deterministic removal and search/replace
Feature-13 migration already moved internal code to canonical names

preFlightChecklist: Confirm no active consumers rely on legacy module/CLI names
Confirm public documentation has advertised cutoff date
Create release note section specifically for breaking changes
Prepare rollback patch that reintroduces shims if needed
